{{Short description|UK based reintroduction expert and author}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2022}}

'''Derek Gow''' (born 29 June 1965) is a UK-based [[Species reintroduction|reintroduction]] expert, farmer and author<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 September 2020|title=An interview with Derek Gow: Bringing Back the Beaver|url=https://www.nhbs.com/blog/an-interview-with-derek-gow-bringing-back-the-beaver|access-date=2021-10-28|website=www.nhbs.com|language=en}}</ref> known for his work with [[European water vole|watervoles]], [[white stork]]s, [[European wildcat|wildcats]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=4 September 2020|title='It's going to be our way now': the guerrilla rewilder shaking up British farming|url=http://www.theguardian.com/environment/2020/sep/04/its-going-to-be-our-way-now-the-guerrilla-rewilder-shaking-up-british-farming-aoe|access-date=2021-10-27|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref> and Eurasian [[Eurasian beaver|beavers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bringing Back the Beaver - Chelsea Green Publishing |url=https://www.chelseagreen.com/product/bringing-back-the-beaver-pb/ |access-date=2023-12-27 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He also imported the first [[Heck cattle]] to the UK. However, after aggressive behaviour could harm or even kill handlers, a significant proportion of the herd was culled.<ref>{{Cite web|date=5 January 2015|title=Devon farmer forced to offload aggressive Nazi-bred 'super cows'|url=http://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/jan/05/devon-farmer-forced-offload-nazi-bred-super-cows|access-date=2021-10-28|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=9 January 2015|title=British farmer forced to destroy herd of 'aggressive' Nazi-bred super|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/climate-change/news/british-farmer-forced-to-turn-half-his-murderous-herd-of-nazi-cows-into-sausages-9958988.html|access-date=2021-10-28|website=The Independent|language=en}}</ref>

Born in [[Dundee]], he left school when he was 17 and worked in agriculture for five years. Inspired by the writing of [[Gerald Durrell]], he jumped at the chance to manage a European wildlife park in central Scotland in the late 1990s before moving on to develop two nature centres in England. Gow owns a 400 acre farm ([[Rewilding Coombeshead]]) in [[Lifton, Devon|Lifton]], Devon, which is home to captive breeding facilities for native flora and fauna, visitor accommodation and a working farm.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derek Gow |url=https://chelseagreen.co.uk/cg-author/derek-gow/ |access-date=2023-12-27 |website=Chelsea Green UK |language=en-GB}}</ref> Much of the land is under the process of [[Rewilding (conservation biology)|rewilding]], like the [[Knepp Wildland|Knepp Estate]].  The farm is home to many species, including [[Eurasian lynx]], [[wild boar]], [[Eurasian beaver|beavers]], [[White stork|white storks]], [[black stork]]s, [[European tree frog|common tree frogs]], and harvest mice.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-06-05|title=Wildcats, storks and beavers: my stay on a Devon rewilding farm|url=http://www.theguardian.com/travel/2021/jun/05/my-stay-at-a-devon-rewilding-farm-wildlife-holiday|access-date=2021-10-28|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-03|title=Can Britain’s long lost tree frogs bounce back?|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/tree-frogs-rewilding-biodiversity-beavers-b1797072.html|access-date=2021-10-28|website=The Independent|language=en}}</ref>
